en: The waling-waling, known as the Queen of Philippine Orchids, is a rare epiphytic plant biologically endemic only to the island of Mindanao.
The 2,000-year-old Ifugao Rice Terraces use an ancient, gravity-driven irrigation system that channels rainwater from mountain forests down to the agricultural terraces.
The Philippine eagle, our national bird, has a shaggy crest and is scientifically classified as Pithecophaga jefferyi, meaning monkey-eating eagle.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfect conical shape, which geologists attribute to repeated layers of highly viscous lava flows.
Farmers in the Cordillera region selectively cultivate multiple varieties of heirloom rice, such as tinawon, to biologically adapt to high-altitude climates.
The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, is biologically distinct from the national animal, the carabao, due to its shorter height and V-shaped horns.
Modern giant Parol lanterns in San Fernando use LED bulbs wired in parallel electrical circuits, ensuring the whole display stays lit if one bulb fails.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a complex karst limestone landscape formed by millions of years of continuous chemical water erosion.
The Tagbanua people of Palawan harvest wild honey by using smoke that biologically masks honeybee alarm pheromones, preventing the insects from stinging.
The eight-rayed sun on the Philippine flag represents the first eight provinces, and its rays are geometrically spaced at exact 45-degree intervals.
Dr. Fe del Mundo pioneered the use of bamboo incubators to medically treat premature babies in rural areas without relying on expensive electricity.
The traditional Filipino food balut is created by incubating fertilized duck eggs at a biologically optimal 37.5 degrees Celsius for 18 days before boiling.
